sections.html:
Safford is where you pay. The County Treasurer collects for all nineteen taxing authorities in the county from the General Services Building, 921 Thatcher Blvd.

  • In person: cash, checks, and credit or debit cards are taken at the counter.
  • By mail: P.O. Box 747, Safford, AZ 85548.
  • Drop box: in the east parking lot of the General Services Building.
  • Online: Point and Pay adds a convenience fee of 2.45 percent for credit cards (minimum $2.00), $1.50 for an electronic check, or $3.95 for a debit card.

Call the Treasurer at 928-428-3440 to confirm an amount due, and the Assessor at 928-428-2828 for valuation questions. The Treasurer's online tax search refreshes hourly on business days and shows balances and lien redemption amounts.

Each September the county mails one statement with two stubs, one per half. A late date that falls on a weekend or holiday shifts to the next business day.

Next up is the second half, due March 1, 2027. May 1, 2027 falls on a Saturday, so that half is late after 5 p.m. on Monday, May 3. A first half still open today is already accruing interest.

Payment or chargeRule
First halfDue October 1; late after 5 p.m. on November 1
Second halfDue March 1; late after 5 p.m. on May 1
Whole yearPaid by December 31, no interest is assessed
Bills under $100Due by December 31
Interest16 percent simple per year, added monthly on the first (A.R.S. 42-18053)
Tax lien saleEach February, covering the previous cycle's delinquent taxes

You can pay in pieces, monthly or twice a month, but interest keeps building on whatever past-due amount is left.

sections.h2: If your tax bill never arrives
sections.html:
Tax and interest are owed whether or not the paper bill shows up. Not receiving a statement is no ground for waiving interest, and A.R.S. 42-18054 treats liability for tax, interest, fees and penalties the same way.

If no bill has reached you by October 1, call 928-428-3440 for the amount. Compare the parcel number and description on each statement with your own records before paying, so the money lands on the right property. Owners with a mortgage should confirm that the lender requested the bill. Many lenders pull tax data straight from the county and the owner then gets an informational postcard. A lender that does not make the request leaves the statement to go to the owner.

Owners of record get a Notice of Valuation from the Assessor in the mail before March 1 each year. Since Proposition 117 took effect for tax year 2015, the Limited Property Value is the only figure used to calculate the tax, and it can rise no more than 5 percent per year.

This changes how you appeal. The tax rests on the Limited Property Value, but the only number you can contest is the Full Cash Value, the market-based one. State law produces the limited figure from last year's value or a formula, so it offers nothing to argue.

Rates are the other half of the bill. Each taxing authority on your parcel, from the county to your school district, sets its own rate, and A.R.S. 42-17151 requires levies to be fixed on or before the third Monday in August. The Treasurer's page lists current rates by taxing authority and combined rates by area. Use the Treasurer's Office for balances and due dates and the Assessor's Office for values.

Your appeal starts with a petition to the Assessor. File it inside 60 days of the notice date shown on the front of the Notice of Valuation. That deadline comes from A.R.S. 42-16051, which also wants your estimate of full cash value and the facts behind it.

Pick the form that matches your property from the list on the county's Assessment and Appeals page:

  • DOR 82130R for residential property.
  • DOR 82130 for commercial, industrial, vacant land and agricultural property.
  • DOR 82131 for multiple parcels, and DOR 82130NC for a Notice of Change.
  • DOR 82130AA if you want an agent to act for you.
  • DOR 82300 and its supplements, for commercial appeals based on income and expense statements.

When the Assessor's answer leaves you unsatisfied, the next stop can be the Board of Equalization, the Tax Court, or both, and the original appeal may also be filed directly with the Tax Court. Your decision letter from the Assessor names the next deadline, so open it as soon as it comes.

Arizona gives breaks to widows and widowers, to people with a total and permanent disability, and to honorably discharged people who served and now have a disability, plus a Senior Freeze. The County Assessor runs each one. Each exemption trims taxable value by a fixed dollar amount, and every individual exemption has a household income limit.

  • Only one individual exemption can be claimed, even by someone who fits several categories.
  • The veteran exemption changed beginning with tax years that start on or after January 1, 2026, and a new veteran application goes to the Assessor between the first Monday in January and March 1.
  • The Senior Freeze fixes the valuation of a primary residence for a renewable three years when the owner meets age and income rules. Taxes are still levied at the district rate.

Dollar limits change every year. Ask the Graham County Assessor at 928-428-2828 for this year's amounts and forms.

Each February the Treasurer sells delinquent taxes to an investor at a lien sale. Bidders compete on the lowest interest rate they will accept, and the winner receives a registered Certificate of Purchase.

The parcel list is posted outside the Treasurer's office, advertised in the Eastern Arizona Courier, and updated weekly in February on the county website. A lien buyer must also take assignment of any older outstanding certificates on the parcel. Anyone who owes back tax can get the exact payoff figure by calling 928-428-3440.

sections.h2: Selling a house in Graham County
sections.html:
Your title company decides who covers the current year's tax. The next statement generally lands in the buyer's name about a year after the deed is recorded, and depending on the closing date, the current year's tax may not have been assessed yet.

A titled mobile home is billed as personal property. The tax record moves only after the buyer is issued a new title, and a signature on the back of the old title leaves the roll untouched. Complete the title transfer so the following bill reaches the right person.

With a balance due, get a payoff figure from the Treasurer and hand it to the title company, which pays it out of your proceeds. A cash buyer is not waiting on a lender, so a clean tax record protects that speed.

Before you put the house on the market, spend a few minutes on the tax side. Look up your parcel in the Treasurer's search and note the balance and any redemption amount. Check the notice date on your latest Notice of Valuation so you know whether the appeal window is still open. If you hold an exemption or the Senior Freeze, ask the Assessor how a sale changes it. Then give your title company the Treasurer's phone number so the payoff request can go out the day you sign the contract.

Part of the San Carlos Apache Indian Reservation lies in Graham County, whose seat and largest city is Safford. Thatcher and Pima are the other towns. About 40,157 people live here, in 14,645 housing units. A typical owner-occupied home was valued at $212,000 for 2020 through 2024, owners live in 73.1 percent of homes, and median household income was $67,325.

faqs.q: What interest does Graham County charge on late property tax?
faqs.a: Sixteen percent per year, simple, added month by month. Clear the full year before December 31 and no interest applies. A bill you never received does not excuse it.

faqs.q: Can I make partial payments on my Graham County taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The Treasurer accepts partial payments monthly, semi-monthly or on your own schedule. Interest keeps building on whatever past-due balance remains.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Graham County valuation?
faqs.a: Sixty days from the notice date on the front of your Notice of Valuation. The notice is mailed before March 1 each year.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to pay Graham County property tax online?
faqs.a: Yes. Point and Pay adds 2.45 percent to a credit card payment ($2.00 minimum), $1.50 to an electronic check and $3.95 to a debit card. The counter, the mail and the drop box carry no such fee.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Graham County tax balance?
faqs.a: The Treasurer's Office at 928-428-3440 handles balances, due dates and payment options. Call the Assessor at 928-428-2828 for values, exemptions and appeal forms.
